summary: Builder 'guards' (second run after the container restart: the first run's patch was applied and carried on). Behaviour tests now cover every 0.8.2 gap in the guarding code (23 bugs). Outside it, new tests cover six gaps or lost catches (M002, M055, M057, M059, M111, M155), and M060 is now caught by an existing test that is listed for it. M005 and M006, the two line gaps, were already caught by part A's test_line_rules. The digest rule holds: on a stale seed, the window modules pass and exactly one test fails, test_project_desk.Seed.test_the_seed_of_this_tree_is_current, and its message gives the commands that make the seed current. The planted bugs were run again with the seed made current before each bug. Guarding code: 30 of 53 caught by behaviour at 0.8.2 (56.6%), 51 of 53 now (96.2%). The other two (M093, M096) make packaging refuse the planted tree, so they ran on a stale seed and were caught by tests other than the seed-current one, which makes 53 of 53 if counted. Overall: 70 of 131 (53.4%) before, 100 of 131 (76.3%) now. The 26 other gaps that were not rerun are counted as still missed. The rerun is repeatable with tools/planted_bugs (plant.py, run.py, bugs.json with verdict_0_8_2 and verdict_0_8_4, README). It never ships: package_graphite has NOT_SHIPPED, and test_release_check.Kit pins it. All 19 touched or importing modules pass in the default and Kasandra looks.

Machine time (19 Nov 23:57 to 20 Nov 00:47 UTC, never more than two test processes): touched modules 6.2 min per look x 2; guarding rerun 7.8 min wall, 936 worker-seconds for 64 bugs; other rerun 16.5 min wall, about 1,890 worker-seconds for 52 bugs; follow-ups (M002/M055/M060 again, stale-seed checks, last module checks) about 10 min. About 47 minutes in all, a little over the 40-minute budget because of the follow-ups.

Digest rule. A comment appended to workbench/engineering_kernel.py makes seed_status STALE. Then test_desk_acts gives 30 OK and test_project_desk gives 14 run, 1 failed, and that one is the seed-current test. In the first run, with the same kind of stale seed, test_context_menu passed all 44 and test_desk_scenes all 5 with the hold. Without it they had 2 and 5 failures. A comment in desk_doers.py does not make the seed stale, because desk_doers.py is not a seed input.

Results are in work/b084b/guards/final_guarding.jsonl, final_other.jsonl, final_extra.jsonl (M002, M055) and final_m060.jsonl. bugs.json records verdict_0_8_4: 109 caught, 2 caught_on_stale_seed, 5 missed, 40 not rerun.
decisions: run.py makes the seed current with tools/package_graphite.py --manifest-only only, and does not record docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json again. The registry records operations and the code that serves each, not source bytes, so when LiveRecord fails on a planted bug the behaviour of the live foundation changed. M092, M094 and M095 are counted as caught that way. Re-recording the registry would hide that change.

When packaging refuses a planted tree, the bug runs on the stale seed. Every failure counts except test_project_desk.Seed.test_the_seed_of_this_tree_is_current, and the report lists the bug apart (M093, M096). The headline numbers set these two apart, and I also give the figure that counts them.

Digest rule: the program's own refusal is unchanged. In tests only, the window modules (test_desk_acts.build_window, which test_desk_scenes uses, and test_context_menu.setUpModule) read an edited, unpackaged seed (STALE or SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) as bound, keeping its real seed_id. The Kernel modules already did this. An absent or broken seed still refuses. The one place that says the seed is stale is test_project_desk.Seed.test_the_seed_of_this_tree_is_current. This was a small change, so I made it rather than putting it in not_done.

Two new modules, each where no module fitted: test_record_paths (record_io had none) and test_viewer_kinds (universal_view and the view modules had none). Each is in FOCUSED_MODULES on its own line with its own comment, after test_resource_rules.

The M020 test does not build a whole adaptive investigation, which needs a problem, a model binding and a live model. It writes the stored order as the adaptive controller leaves it (profile and current job), then calls the real work.pause/work.revoke and the real jobs.cancel.

M055 is in the 'other' group because files_service is not on the guarding list, but it guards the owner's files. Its test is in test_change_sets because the refusal tells the caller to propose the change instead.
M060 needed no new test: test_line_rules already tests files_service.number but was missing from the bug's module list in bugs.json. I put it first there.
bugs.json keeps the 0.8.2 verdicts, ids and layout. It adds verdict_0_8_4, so a later release can compare bug by bug and see if a retired test lowered the rate.
The take test went into a new class TheBounds, not TheSevenFaults, because that class holds the seven line faults from part A.
The README example uses COPY_A/COPY_B placeholders, so there is no absolute path anywhere in tools/planted_bugs.
not_done: M071 local_brain._start_server: the fallback process.kill() after kill_owned. Under the simulator, FakePopen.wait() kills the process itself, so the fallback cannot be seen. Catching it needs a FakePopen whose wait() only waits, with kill_owned patched to do nothing. It was not in the 0.8.2 valid set.
M075 model_settings.snapshot, '>' to '>=' on the journal budget (void at 0.8.2): missed. It needs a test whose job records add up to exactly MAX_JOURNAL bytes, all listed and not marked partial.
M063 line_steps.preview_columns 'long column' threshold of 24 (boundary): missed. It needs a line preview with a column that averages exactly 24 characters.
M150 stac_bridge.compile_program 4,096-byte bound (boundary): missed. It needs a program of exactly 4,096 bytes accepted and one of 4,097 refused.

M114 change_sets_qt.ChangesTab.reload, 'is' to 'is not': caught at 0.8.2 by test_every_navigation_changes_nothing ('No app office in the Apps list'), missed now on a current seed. That catch was probably a seed-digest failure counted as behaviour. It needs a window test that opens Changes after a proposal and checks the list shows it.

M043, M045, M046 (field_page): Field window tests for the face signal, a refused office read, and leaving the Field after an open. M142 (field_doubt.doubts_for): the doubts list of a Rail Demo sheet. release_note: 0.8.4 checks its own tests by planting small bugs in the code and counting how many the tests catch. In the code that protects you (Kasandra's hand, the Kernel's permissions and record paths, the memory and model rules, change sets and undo, continuing work, the seed and release checks), the tests caught 30 of 53 at 0.8.2. They now catch 51, which is 96%, and the remaining two make packaging refuse to build. Across all 131 planted bugs the rate rose from 53% to 76%. A window test no longer fails just because the seed is out of date: one test says so and gives the command that fixes it. The rerun lives in tools/planted_bugs, so each release can report its own number, and it is never shipped.
